Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Zimbabwe's reply.
... SECOND INNINGS ...

For Zimbabwe, Wellington Masakadza and Blessing Muzarabani did the bulk of the damage with three wickets apiece, while Victor Nyauchi set the tone early with his double strike. It’s a lively surface offering good pace, bounce, and movement off the deck, which means the Zimbabwean openers will be tested right from the outset. Bangladesh will be eager to strike a few early blows and finish the day on a high. Back in a bit for the tourists' response.

For Bangladesh, both Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mominul Haque got starts, but neither could convert them into a substantial score. The batting unit, overall, left much to be desired, with some questionable shot selection. That said, credit must go to Zimbabwe, who were disciplined with the ball for the most part and capitalised on every opening. Hasan Mahmud and Jaker Ali showed some resistance on either side of the Tea break, but their efforts weren’t enough to guide Bangladesh to a respectable total.

Bangladesh have been bowled out for just 191! It’s been a dramatic collapse of significant proportions. From a promising position at 98/2, the hosts lost their remaining 8 wickets for only 93 runs. Zimbabwe will be absolutely delighted with their effort, especially losing the toss. It’s been a spirited performance with the ball, and they will be keen to make the most of this advantage with the bat.

... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

From a solid position at 98/2, Bangladesh slipped to 146/7 in no time. Jaker Ali, however, managed to survive till the end of the session, with Hasan Mahmud for company. A lot will now rest on Jaker’s shoulders to steer the hosts to a respectable total. As for Zimbabwe, they couldn’t have asked for a better session. They will be eager to return with the same intensity and wrap up the innings quickly. Back in a bit for the third and final session of the day.

After a brief rain delay, the second session got underway with both sides holding their ground and not giving an inch. Zimbabwe's bowlers adjusted their lengths smartly, pitching it up more often and forcing the batters to play. Mominul Haque and Najmul Hossain Shanto survived a few plays and misses, but managed to hang in until Shanto perished. That wicket opened the door for the visitors, and they charged right through it with Wellington Masakadza leading the charge for them.

SESSION SUMMARY - 26 overs, 70 runs and 5 wickets. Zimbabwe’s session through and through, and it’s the visitors who will enjoy a much sweeter cup of Tea between the two sides. Bangladesh find themselves in a hole, some of it dug by their own undoing, particularly with questionable shot selection.

Muzarabani and Ngarava bowled much better in their second spell and created several nervy moments for both Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mominul Haque. Mominul had a big let-off when he was dropped on a duck, but despite the pressure, the experienced pair held firm and went into the break unscathed. There was consistent movement off the surface throughout the first session, and with overcast conditions expected to persist, the pacers will remain in the game for most of the day. As for Shanto and Mominul, they will have to reset and start afresh after the interval on a pitch that is still doing plenty. Do join us back at 6.40 am GMT for the start of the second session.

After losing the toss, Zimbabwe's new-ball pair of Blessing Muzarabani and Richard Ngarava couldn’t quite trouble the Bangladeshi openers. They were guilty of bowling a touch too short and failed to make the most of the helpful surface and overcast conditions. It was Victor Nyauchi, introduced as the first change, who showed the right way forward. By pitching it up and inviting the drive, he found immediate success, removing both openers and injecting life back into the Zimbabwean effort.

An attritional session of Test cricket comes to an end! Zimbabwe will walk off with a hint of disappointment, knowing they could have picked up at least one more wicket after removing both openers. Bangladesh, on the other hand, will be relieved to have survived the session with just two wickets down in testing conditions.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! The first 40 minutes or so belonged to Bangladesh, but the introduction of Victor Nyauchi has helped Zimbabwe pull things back slightly. It could have been even better had Nyasha Mayavo held onto the catch offered by Mominul Haque in the previous over. Both Blessing Muzarabani and Richard Ngarava weren’t quite full enough with their lengths early on, but Nyauchi has shown what’s needed, and it remains to be seen if the others can follow suit. As for Bangladesh, they have two seasoned campaigners at the crease now and will be hoping to navigate the remainder of the session without any further setbacks.
